test_title: PYST 9: SSC CGL 2025 Tier-I Similar Paper - General Awareness (Held On: 14th Sep 2025 Shift 3)
subject: gk
question: Under Article 262, what best describes Parliament’s authority regarding inter-State water disputes?

options.text: It can legislate only on navigation but not restrict SC role
It may establish water tribunals and restrict Supreme Court review
It can dissolve State water bodies permanently
It mandates Inter-State Council mediation first

solution:
The correct answer is __**It may establish water tribunals and restrict Supreme Court review**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 262** of the **Constitution of India** deals with the adjudication of disputes relating to the waters of inter-State rivers or river valleys.
 
• It empowers the **Parliament** to make laws to prevent or settle disputes concerning inter-State water resources.
 
• Under **Article 262(1)**, Parliament can legislate to provide for the adjudication of such disputes. *Hence, statement is correct.*
 
• **Article 262(2)** allows Parliament to restrict or exclude the jurisdiction of the **Supreme Court or any other court** concerning inter-State water disputes.
 
• This provision ensures that disputes are handled through specialized tribunals rather than through regular judicial processes. *Hence, statement is correct.*
 
• **The Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956** was enacted under Article 262 to establish tribunals for resolving such disputes. Tribunals like the **Cauvery Water Dispute Tribunal** have been established under this Act.
 
• Such tribunals have the authority to make binding decisions to resolve disputes among states. *Hence, statement is correct.*
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is It may establish water tribunals and restrict Supreme Court review.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Overview of Article 262:**

 
 
• **Article 262** provides Parliament with exclusive powers to legislate on the adjudication of disputes regarding inter-State river waters.
 
• It enables Parliament to establish tribunals specifically designed to handle such disputes, ensuring the resolution is efficient and specialized.
 
 
 
• **The Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956:**
 
 
• This Act operationalizes Article 262 by providing a framework for creating tribunals to adjudicate inter-State water disputes.
 
• Tribunals established under this Act are empowered to make binding decisions that cannot be challenged in courts, including the Supreme Court.
 
• **Example:** The **Cauvery Water Dispute Tribunal** was formed to resolve disputes between Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Kerala, and Puducherry.
 
 
 
• **Supreme Court’s Restricted Role:**
 
 
• Article 262 allows Parliament to exclude the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court, ensuring disputes are handled solely through specialized tribunals.
 
• This provision streamlines the resolution process by bypassing lengthy judicial procedures.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Tribunals under Article 262:**

 
 
• Tribunals established under the Inter-State River Water Disputes Act are designed to resolve disputes efficiently and impartially.
 
• Their decisions are binding and cannot be challenged in courts, ensuring finality in resolution.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Tribunals:**
 
 
• **Cauvery Water Dispute Tribunal:** Resolving disputes between Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Kerala, and Puducherry.
 
• **Krishna Water Dispute Tribunal:** Addressing disputes between Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra, and Karnataka.
